title: Dependency Anticipation Lifecycle and Service Contracts
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: We frequently discover cross-team blockers late in the cycle (T-2 weeks) causing scope cuts or hotfix cycles. There is no lightweight, enforceable 'service contract' between teams outlining minimal readiness signals and fallbacks for each release window.

Goal: Define a Dependency Anticipation Lifecycle (DAL) that combines: 1) a short machine-readable service contract for each deliverable, 2) a gating checklist evaluated at three timeboxes (T-8, T-4, T-1 weeks), and 3) an escalation/fallback catalog (what to ship with degraded integration). Deliverables: service contract spec, gating checklist templates, automation in the Roadmap Readiness dashboard to surface contracts that are expiring/unfulfilled, and a runbook for PM/ENG/design leads for last-mile negotiation.

Scope: Focus on cross-team dependencies that affect GA releases and Dedicated/Private features (security or infra changes). Out of scope: purely research spikes and experiments not on the release plan.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Service contract schema published in Confluence and an example populated for 4 active initiatives.
2) Roadmap Readiness dashboard surfaces contract compliance status for each initiative (T-8/T-4/T-1).
3) Two automation alerts wired to Slack #release-ops for breached contracts at T-4 and T-1.
4) A documented fallback catalog with at least one fallback per major integration and signoff from Eng/Design/Security for one pilot release.
